items.entity: Aspect ratio of the analysed (right-half) MBB design domain
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives Lx:Ly = 6:1, and Fig. 2a puts F at Lx/2, so Lx looks like the full span and the optimized right half would be 3:1. But Sec. 4.1.1 gives a 180x30 (6:1) grid for 'the domain' and then says only the right symmetric half is optimized. If that grid is taken as the half, the half is 6:1 and the full beam 12:1.
readings: Analysed half is 3:1 (full beam 6:1; Lx is the full span)
Analysed half is 6:1 (full beam 12:1; Lx:Ly applied to the modelled half)

items.entity: Element grid of the optimized half model
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says 'Nex = 180 and Ney = 30 ... The right symmetric half section is optimized' but does not say whether 180x30 is the full beam or the analysed half. App. B gets the same gSF m = 1 result as Table 2 (f0 = 0.0149, Mnd = 1.57%) with '90 x 30 quad finite elements ... symmetric half design domain'. App. B.1 uses '180 x 60' for 'the MBB design domain'.
readings: 90 x 30 square Q4 elements on the half (180 x 30 is the full beam)
180 x 30 square Q4 elements on the half
180 x 30 Q4 elements over a 3:1 half (non-square elements, width:height = 1:2)

items.entity: End support of the simply supported beam (outer bottom end of the half model)
items.description: The text only says 'simply supported beam' (Sec. 4.1) and mentions a 'roller support' (Sec. 4.1.1). Where the support sits and how many nodes it covers are only shown in Fig. 2a, which is not available.
readings: Single node at the outer bottom corner of the half (y = 0, x = 1.0 of the half-length from the symmetry line)
Short patch of bottom-edge nodes at the outer end (about the last 2-3 elements, 0.97-1.0 of the half-length, y = 0)

items.entity: Restraints of the half model (symmetry edge and outer support)
items.description: The half-model boundary conditions are never written out. Sec. 4.1.1 mentions a 'roller support' for the half designs (1-3 materials) but 'roller and hinge support' for the full-beam designs (also in Sec. 4.5.1). Which end of the full beam is hinged, and what the outer support of the right half becomes, is only in Fig. 2a. The symmetry restraint on the cut edge is implied by 'right symmetric half', not stated.
readings: ux = 0 on all nodes of the symmetry (cut) edge + roller (uy = 0 only) at the outer bottom support
ux = 0 on all nodes of the symmetry edge + hinge (ux = uy = 0) at the outer bottom support

items.entity: Downward point load at the top node of the symmetry edge (half model)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives F = 10^-3 'unit' at the midpoint of the upper edge of the full beam. It does not say whether the half model takes the full F or F/2 on the shared symmetry-line node, so it is also unclear whether the reported f0 (0.0149) refers to the half or the full beam.
readings: F = 1e-3 applied to the half model
F/2 = 5e-4 applied to the half model (full-beam load split by symmetry)

items.description: No Poisson's ratio is given anywhere in the paper. Sec. 4 only normalizes E = 1 for the stiffest material, which is the single material for the 1D SF.
Sec. 3.1 only calls Emin 'a very small stiffness assigned to the void regions/elements'. No value is given.
readings: Emin = 1e-9 (with E = 1)
Emin = 1e-6
Emin = 1e-3

items.description: Sec. 4 says bilinear quadrilateral elements are used but never says whether the 2D analysis is plane stress or plane strain.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2D MBB model. It affects only the size of the strain energy.
readings: Another constant t (f0 scales as 1/t)

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 sets rmin = 3.6, and Eqs. 27-28 use centre-to-centre element distances. The paper gives no absolute Lx, Ly or element size (only the 6:1 ratio), so it never says that rmin is measured in element widths.
readings: rmin = 3.6 element edge lengths (unit-size elements)
rmin = 3.6 in physical length units of an assumed absolute domain size (the same as above only if the element edge is 1)

items.entity: Filter/projection configuration of the Table 2, m = 1 runs (CASE I/II/III)
items.description: Table 2's m = 1 row has three runs, each defined in a single phrase in Sec. 4.1.1: CASE I 'No density filtering', CASE II 'With density filtering', CASE III 'With density and projection filters'. It is not stated whether CASE I uses the beta-continuation projection on unfiltered variables, or whether CASE II keeps rmin = 3.6. The projection settings (eta = 0.5, beta from 1 to 32, doubled every 75 iterations) are given only as general Sec. 4.1.1 settings.
readings: CASE III: density filter (rmin = 3.6) + tanh projection (eta = 0.5, beta 1 -> 32, doubled every 75 iterations); reported f0 = 0.0149, Mnd = 1.57%
CASE II: density filter (rmin = 3.6) only, no projection; reported f0 = 0.0263
CASE I: no filter and no projection; reported f0 = 0.0172
CASE I alternative: no density filter, but tanh projection with the same beta continuation

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 gives no starting design. Sec. 4.4.2 shows that the starting design changes the topology, and Sec. 4.4.3 and Tables 8-9 use xi = 0 elsewhere. Eq. 4 (x11 = -1, x12 = 1) and Sec. 2.1.2 (x11 = 1, x12 = -1) disagree on which vertex is the void, so the sign of a start that matches the volume fraction is also unclear.
readings: xi = 0 in every element (uniform rho = 0.5)
Uniform rho = vf = 0.3 (xi = -0.4 or +0.4, depending on vertex labelling)
Random/perturbed start

items.description: MMA [43] is named in Sec. 3.3, with at most 400 iterations (Sec. 4). No move limit, asymptote settings or a0/a_i/c_i/d_i constants are given. The paper's design variables are xi in [-1, 1] (range 2), so any move limit in xi is halved when expressed in density.
readings: Svanberg-default MMA (asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7, a0 = 1, a_i = 0, c_i = 1000, d_i = 1), no extra move limit
Default MMA plus an external move limit of 0.1-0.2 on rho (0.2-0.4 on xi)

items.description: Sec. 3.3 and Sec. 4 give nf = min(10/obj, 1x10^2)|loop=1 in garbled form, said to be applied 'in every iteration'. It is unclear whether nf is fixed from the iteration-1 objective or recomputed each iteration, and whether the reported f0 values (e.g., 0.0149) include nf. This affects MMA scaling and how results can be compared.
readings: nf = min(10/f0 at iteration 1, 100), held constant; reported f0 includes nf
nf = min(10/f0 at iteration 1, 100), held constant; reported f0 is the unscaled 0.5*U^T K U
nf recomputed every iteration as min(10/f0, 100)
No normalization

items.description: Sec. 4 gives only a maximum of 400 MMA iterations, with no tolerance on design change or objective. With beta doubled every 75 iterations (Sec. 4.1.1), beta = 32 is reached only at about iteration 375.
readings: Always run the full 400 MMA iterations
Stop earlier once beta = 32 and the max design change falls below a tolerance (e.g., 0.01)

locator: Sec. 4.1.1, the 2-D MBB beam, single-material case (Table 2, m = 1)
